title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 11
text: This content contains vulgar language. Please avoid viewing this while eating.
The good-for-nothing dad of the Robin Hood-like thief runs toward the workshop. I follow slowly behind him. Then I take a look inside the workshop.

It has a different vibe from Rat’s lab. Well, that place prioritizes monster research, so it’s more of a proper research facility. This one, with its cauldrons and all, feels more like a witch’s house—a real workshop. Hmm… I guess an alchemist’s workshop is easier to picture these days. Deep inside that workshop, the Robin Hood-type old man is fiddling with something, making a clattering racket.
“Watch this! You’ll be speechless when you see my latest creation!”
“Whatever you show me, I don’t think it’ll be anything special.”
Honestly, this guy is lacking in all sorts of ways. I know it’s a bit much of me to talk down to him like this, but the things he makes have a fatal flaw.
It’s demand. He completely ignores what buyers actually want. Earthy truffle chocolates, chocolates wrapped in banana peels—only eccentric people would want those.

…Even someone as crazy as me understands that much, don’t you think? After all, the villagers were happy with the bread tree and the crepe tree, and there are even people who come by to buy them from time to time. Raph-chan was a product that had completely discarded that kind of thinking, but in the end, she turned out to be a valuable asset. The Raph-species itself is a pretty excellent combat force even among monsters, after all.
There’s no way I could ever create something like that based on this guy’s ideas. Even Rat was impressed, wasn’t he? He said he couldn’t find a single flaw.
Eventually, the Robin Hood-like old man must have finished fiddling with his invention, because he reached for the cloth covering it.
“Behold!”

The cloth was yanked away. Seeing what was there, I furrowed my brow and tilted my head. A device modeled after the lower half of a horse-shaped monster? The front half was a transparent beaker for holding ingredients? And it was connected to the lower half. The beaker was filled to the brim with chocolate.
“This is the second prototype of my latest creation!”

With a click, the Robin Hood-like old man pressed a button located near the thigh of the horse’s lower body. There was a clang, and a rhythm like that of a steam engine began to resonate. Then, the chocolate inside the front half started rattling about, shrinking in volume as it flowed toward the lower body. This… gives me a very bad feeling!
“Raphtalia! Close your eyes and cover your ears!”
“Huh? Oh, okay!”
It must have been right as I heeded her warning and closed my eyes and covered my ears just as she ordered.
B… Bbbb… From here on, I’ll intentionally describe it as the murmur of a river.
From a certain hole in the lower half… a fist-sized chunk of chocolate fell out and bounced on the floor. Just as she’d said, everyone present was left speechless. In the worst possible way.
“This is my brand-new invention! Horse-shit chocolate! Well, aren’t you moved to tears by my invention?!”
“Die! You scat-loving bastard!”
This shitty old man seriously never makes anything decent! Even earthy truffle chocolate or banana-skin-only chocolate would be better than this.
“Just shut up and eat the chocolate—”
Just then, two shadows approached the old bastard and slammed their fists into the horse-manure-chocolate-making machine.
“Hmph!”
“Aaaaaah!”
The shadows turned out to be the Robin Hood’s mother and younger sister. The machine took the brunt of their blows, crashed into the wall, belched out a cloud of smoke, and came to a halt.
“My great invention! What are you doing?!”
“Give it a rest already! Who’s supposed to eat that?!”
“Exactly! What’s the fun in wasting food?!”

I have to admit, they have a point. There’s no way we’re eating that. Would Filo eat it? Nah, even Filo wouldn’t touch that. If she did, her idol career would be over. I’d wipe her out of the industry without a second thought.
“I’ve put up with this until now, but ever since my father-in-law and mother-in-law passed away, you’ve been doing whatever you want! I’ve had enough!”
“Are you defying my will?! Get out! Don’t ever come back!”
Kicking his family out just because they defied him? What a worthless piece of shit of a father. In every sense of the word.
“My will? Then try eating this chocolate! Go on!”
The Robin Hood’s mother points to the object—which looks like horse-manure chocolate—and orders the shitty old man to eat it.
“What good would it do for me to eat it?! This chocolate is meant for customers!”
Don’t feed that crap to customers! Who’s going to eat that?
“Just eat it already!”
“So why the hell do I have to eat it?!”
“Are you saying you made something you can’t even eat yourself!?”
“Hmph. This horse-manure chocolate will be our breakthrough into a new market!”
“No way in hell—just give it up!”
As they were having this exchange, Raphtalia had opened her eyes and stopped covering her ears without them even noticing.
“Raphtalia, you’re not supposed to open your eyes.”
“I-it’s okay.”
“You mustn’t let something like this get in your eyes! It’ll taint you.”
“Um… well, just by looking at the shape, I can kind of tell what happened…”

Well, it’s easy to imagine, I guess. But he’s gone and made something absolutely outrageous. A “genius the world won’t recognize”… or whatever—he’s probably just full of himself, but this idea won’t catch on even after hundreds or thousands of years. At best, it’s a one-time gag.
Come to think of it… I feel like there was something similar in my world, but it was a finished product. There’s no way they’d let anyone watch the actual creation process.
“Oh well, it’s just Prototype No. 2 anyway. I still have Prototype No. 1.”
With that, that jerk of a dad pulled out another piece of cloth. Underneath was the lower half of a Filolial—
“Guaaaaaa!”
Chick’s sharp kick destroyed Prototype No. 1 of the Horse Manure Chocolate Maker. Good job. That’s exactly what I wanted.
“My greatest invention of the centuryaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
The two prototypes billowed black smoke. Hmph… With this, these foolish inventions have vanished from the face of the earth.
“You lottttt… I’ll never forgive you! So this barbaric act was born out of jealousy of my talent, was it!?”
“How did it come to that?!”
“If you’re so upset, go ahead and bring me something that surpasses my invention!”
“You!”
“Dad!”

My family is completely on my side, too. Honestly, I can’t deal with this. But if I ignore an idiot like this now, he’ll just get even more cocky. Engaging with him won’t lead to anything good, but if the outcome is going to be bad either way, crushing this guy’s pride is at least a little better.
“Fine, then.”
“The Shield Hero!?”
“Naofumi-sama!?　What are you planning to do!?”
“I don’t know if this guy will admit it, but I’m going to show him what kind of things people actually want.”
I pulled a Bread Tree seed out of my pocket. Just seeing that made Raphtalia pull a sour face. I get it. I know Raphtalia hates thinking about what happened back then.
“What are you planning to do?”
“Just watch and see.”

The Bread Tree is an invention I came up with when I was acting crazy, but it’s incredibly well-made. It’s highly expandable—a marvel even Rat would be impressed by. And my shield possesses a skill called “Plant Modification,” and among the skills I acquired after the world achieved peace was one called “Genetic Modification.” Apparently, the shield I held when I went a bit off the rails was a comprehensive one, but fragments of those skills also existed in other shields.

It’s possible to recreate it by gathering enough of those fragments. Among the skills I’ve acquired is one called “Hybrid Synthesis.” This is a handy skill that allows me to determine the direction of crossbreeding, regardless of whether the subjects are plants, animals, or monsters. However, activating it consumes a considerable amount of Magical Power and SP. It would likely take a long time to create something that combines the best traits of both.

But if I have the materials, it’s possible to create something simple. I collected seeds from a nearby chocolate tree and, holding seeds from a bread tree, activated the skill. The thing I need to be careful about is karma, I suppose.

I made the two seeds float and tweaked their stats. Then, just to the right degree… there’s only a fifty-fifty chance this will work out. There’s also a risk of it running amok. In the worst-case scenario, I’ll have Raphtalia and Chick dispose of it.
The Bread Tree seed is based on a Bio-Plant. Because of that, it possesses broad expandability and mutability. I restricted that aspect and injected the Chocolate Tree’s genetic information into it.
“Haaaaaaah!”
A single seed is ejected from the shield along with a burst of light and smoke. I grab the seed.
“It’s done.”
“Naofumi-sama? Please be careful.”
“Yeah, I know.”

I drop the newly created prototype seed onto the ground. Just to be safe, I designed it to wither immediately so it would take effect right away. If it works, I’ll just decide later whether to mass-produce it.

Originally, I’d been wondering if I could use chocolate tree seeds to create a chocolate forest in our village. But right now, more than anything else, I just want to see the look on that damn old man’s face when he admits defeat. The prototype seed that fell to the ground grew rapidly, turning into a tree that bore bread. A hybrid of a bread tree and a chocolate tree… a chocolate bread tree!
“Waaaaaah…”
The Robin Hood’s sister let out a cry of amazement.
“Go ahead and eat it.”
“Is that okay?”
“Yeah, it’s just a prototype… but I think it’ll be fine.”
Judging by the looks of it, the bread that’s grown isn’t very uniform. Some of them are pretty poorly made.
There are ones that are starting to turn into chocolate cornetes, ones that almost became chocolate koppepan, and ones that look like chocolate chip bread. I guess there are limits after all.
Well, even so, it’s far better than horse-manure chocolate. I can say that with certainty.
“If you don’t harvest them soon, they’ll wither, you know?”
“Hahahaha, they won’t wither that quickly—it’s not like they’re anything special!”
“I made them wither on purpose. It’d be a disaster if they caused a biological disaster, you bastard.”
“As expected of the Shield Hero… you’re thinking about the environment!”

Seeing the Robin Hood’s mother clasp her hands together in admiration, the jerk of a dad let out a frustrated groan and clenched his fist. I don’t really think that’s something to get upset about, though…
“Here, try it.”
I toss the botched chocolate bread at the jerk of a dad.
“Who would eat such disgusting bread!”
I agree with that. I’m not really a fan of Keel’s crepes either.
“Then I’ll eat it!”
The Robin Hood’s younger sister brushed it off, picked up the chocolate bun that had fallen to the ground, and stuffed it into her mouth. Well, it didn’t have to be her, though…
“It looks bad, but… it’s delicious.”
“That’s because it’s made from the original variety of your family’s chocolate tree.”
“We can make this a local specialty! Mom!”
“I suppose so. It’s definitely more valuable than this guy’s invention. It seems to bear fruit really quickly, too.”
“There are various issues, like the soil, so it’ll depend on the orders. It’d be dangerous without some fine-tuning, too.”
“Yeah! The Shield Hero is better!”
“Me too!”
“Grr…”

See? This is what a shift in perspective looks like. Rather than some mysterious invention created from nothing that gets rejected, people are satisfied even when you combine existing things to make something new. People often talk about crazy inventors creating things no one has ever seen before, but those are just things our predecessors chose not to do.

Trust is what matters. Something made by the Shield Hero—who saved the world—just feels better somehow than something from an unknown manufacturer who’s seen as someone who only makes weird stuff. Regardless of the actual quality, of course.
“Well, the downside is that chocolate bread isn’t exactly rare around here, is it?”
“Grr…”
Looking thoroughly annoyed, that jerk of an old man—who’s now on the defensive—is glaring at me. He’s got that same sense of superiority he used to have when he was bullying Trashes back in the day.
“I’m confident in my speed, at least. If you want, I could probably even make the chocolate ripen faster.”
“Wow!”
The Robin Hood-like thief’s little sister praises me in a way that’s clearly meant to show off.
“But… it’s dangerous if they mutate, and there’s the issue of compatibility, too… The finished chocolate might end up being dangerous, so I’ll hold off for now.”
“Ehh! But you’re really thinking about the risks, aren’t you?”
“If we rely too much on Bio-Plants…”
“I know that… but it’s not enough to completely shatter this guy’s pride.”
I pull out another Bio-Plant seed.
“Naofumi-sama, what are you planning to do?”
“This is the end of it.”
Holding the “Truffle Chocolate That Grows in the Field” that my jerk of a dad made, I use the Bio-Plant seeds to perform plant modification, genetic modification, and plant hybridization.
“This is the finished product of the chocolate you’ve been wanting to make, right?”
I made modifications to eliminate the earthy smell, which was the biggest flaw of the “Truffle Chocolate That Grows in the Field.”
“To put it in your terms… ‘Truffle Chocolate That Grows on Trees.’ I’ve fixed the biggest problem—that earthy taste, right?”
I dropped the Truffle Chocolate That Grows on Trees onto the ground to make it bear fruit. With a crackling sound, the improvised seed immediately began to bear fruit.
“Wow… that truffle chocolate has borne fruit, just like a chocolate tree.”
“As long as I have the source material and the ingredients, I can whip something like this up on the spot.”

Well, all in all, it did burn through quite a bit of Magical Power and SP. As for my karma… it’s tilted slightly toward the negative, but it’s no big deal. I can make up for this much in no time. It’s not like I made some earth-shattering modification. I just combined the original ingredients.
“Now then, how long does it take for these so-called truffle chocolates to ripen in the field before they’re ready for harvest?”
“Eight months, Shield Hero!”
“Huh… so it takes quite a while to harvest, doesn’t it? I heard a regular chocolate tree only takes four months.”
“Yes! That’s why we keep warning everyone that it’s inefficient. But they won’t listen.”
“You’ve let a secret slip, you lot!”

That jerk of a dad is giving me a look that says he’s incredibly frustrated. “Classified information”… I mean, every other chocolate farmer knows about this, right? Oh well. People like him just love to blow everything out of proportion. Look, in this world, anyone who refers to themselves as “I” is a total jerk. …Including me.
“With this, we’ve eliminated two weaknesses and created a tree that’s all good points.”
“Yes!　Please, let me have it!”
“Hmm… I wonder what to do…”
I glance briefly at that asshole of a dad.
“If he bows his head, I’ll consider it.”
“You! Haha! Bow your head!”
“Dad! It’d be better for you to rub your head on the ground!”

That’s about what I expected. But my “Robin Hood” mom and sister are so shallow—they always side with the strong… Are they just bitches? Or is it some long-standing grudge? Maybe I should observe them a little longer.

When I look over at that jerk of a dad, his face is so red he looks like he’s about to die of rage, and he’s yelling something or other. I’m trying to point out all his flaws, but his strengths far outweigh them. Even something like this gets refined through trial and error until it’s close to perfection. Probably, truffle chocolates that grow on trees would have issues with taste and other aspects right now. As if I’d just hand it over like that.

But the quality of this guy’s inventions has gone downhill every time they’ve been introduced. In that regard, the truffle chocolates that grow in the fields are actually the better option. Why do they get worse and worse the closer we get to his latest creation? And why did he switch from plant breeding to mechanical engineering in the first place?
“Hmph, hmph! I still have a secret invention concept up my sleeve! Don’t get too cocky over something like that!”
“Here we go again… the guy who starts talking about ‘concepts’ the moment the actual product runs out.”
“Naofumi-sama, if you provoke him too much, this already troublesome situation will only get worse.”
“That’s true, but I want to give this guy a piece of my mind.”
“Sigh… Please keep it to a minimum.”

Hmm… Well, I’ve seen him look frustrated enough, so I guess that’s good enough. For now, I’ll just let him do whatever he wants and then ignore him completely. Just as I was thinking that, that damn old man pulled down a mysterious lever at the back of the workshop.
“Watch this! These are the materials that’ll turn my concept into reality! It’s all part of the prototyping process to perfect the Horse Manure Chocolate!”

With a rumbling “Gogogo,” the workshop floor split in two, and something rose up from below. What is it? What’s he planning to show me this time? If it’s the lower half of a giant horse or something, I’ll have it destroyed on the spot. Just as I was thinking that, a mysterious, giant test tube-like object rose up.

……Huh? Inside the test tube, a monster that looked like a Chocolate Monster was rampaging. I, Raphtalia, the Mother of the Righteous Thieves, my little sister, and Chick all stared blankly, speechless, at what was inside the test tube that had risen up.
“This is it—the boss of the Chocolate Monsters aaaaaaaaaah!”
